unmapped_findings: The TEM dislocation-structure study (Figs. 14–16) for the Fe–30% Al base is reported generically for that composition; the paper states that the ~0.1 at.% B addition caused only a slight increase in flow stress and no significant change in deformation/work-hardening behaviour, so the same substructure is assumed for the Fe–30% Al + 0.1% B sample.

Fe–30% Al (slow-cooled) is described as weakly DO3-ordered; a good degree of DO3 order is expected for alloys containing 25–30% Al, as indicated by strong superlattice spots and coarse DO3 domains in TEM. No evidence of coupled four-partial (perfect DO3) superdislocations was found for any material, including ~30% Al.

Compression tests on the as-cast slow-cooled samples showed a smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points observed, and a slightly curved stress–strain behaviour with no sign of the linear stress–strain regions sometimes reported.

The peak in work hardening rate near 28–29% Al (over the 26–29% Al range) coincides with a maximum in elastic anisotropy (Zener factor A ≈ 6–7 at 28–30% Al); the paper attributes the tendency for dislocations to lie in screw orientations to strong Peierls forces near 25–30% Al rather than to the elastic anisotropy itself.
